 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Jesper Svensson couldn't have picked a better time to deliver one of his strongest rounds of the season.
 With his PGA Tour future hanging in the balance, the Swedish golfer fired an 8-under 64 Thursday to grab the first-round lead at the 2026 RSM Classic, the final tournament of the PGA Tour season at Sea Island Golf Club.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE: Megan Khang Faces LPGA Q-School After Devastating 2026 Season 
 Svensson finished his round on the Plantation Course with four consecutive birdies, building a one-shot advantage over Max Greyserman and Garrick Higgo, who each posted 7-under 65s.
 But this week is about considerably more than winning a golf tournament.
 RSM Classic 2026: Best Bets, Winner Picks, Odds & FedExCup Drama | From the Rough RSM Classic 2026: Best Bets, Winner Picks, Odds & FedExCup Drama | From the RoughRSM CLASSIC 2026 PICKS, PREDICTIONS & BEST BETS! Who wins the PGA Tour's FedExCup Fall finale at Sea Island Golf Club? John Gerber, PGA, and Timm Hamm break ... 
 Svensson entered the event ranked 135th in the FedExCup standings, leaving him well outside the top 100 required to retain full PGA Tour status for 2027. He needs at least a share of second place to reach that critical threshold.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "You can't really deny the situation that you're in," Svensson said. "Not really thinking of it when you're playing as much as trying to hit the right areas and hit some good shots."
 Michael Thorbjornsen, meanwhile, provided one of Thursday's most impressive performances on the more demanding Seaside Course.
 The rising American star, who captured his first PGA Tour victory at the Rocket Classic earlier this year, shot a 6-under 64 despite wet, windy conditions. Five of his seven birdies came from inside 10 feet, providing evidence that recent work on his approach shots is producing results.
 "We've worked very hard on my irons, just having more control," Thorbjornsen said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement His round included five birdies across seven holes surrounding the turn and an important 8-foot par save.
 While Thorbjornsen already owns valuable exemptions into next season's Signature Events, numerous players around him face considerably greater uncertainty.
 Emiliano Grillo, who entered the week 113th in the FedExCup standings, opened with a 66 on the Plantation Course to strengthen his position in the fight for full playing privileges.
 "Everybody knows what they need to do out there," Grillo said.
 Five-time major champion Brooks Koepka also returned to competition after a six-week absence, shooting 67 at Seaside.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Koepka has been working with new coaches, including putting instructor Brad Faxon, as he attempts to rebuild his game.
 Sea Island member Keith Mitchell added a 65 on Seaside, while young contenders Blades Brown and Ben James opened with rounds of 69 and 68, respectively.
 MORE: Scottie Scheffler Stays No. 1 as Tyrrell Hatton Surges in Golf Rankings 
 The tournament continues Friday with players switching courses, including Thorbjornsen and Mitchell moving to the more forgiving Plantation layout.
 For Svensson, the equation is straightforward: Keep making birdies, stay near the top and potentially secure another full season on the PGA Tour.
